Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G1830; not searched out, i.e. (by implication) inscrutable:--unsearchable.
BiblicalUsage: Paul writes of judgments and ways past finding out, and then cries out at the depth of the riches of God's wisdom. The word names what cannot be searched out, the bottom that no sounding line reaches.
TheologicalSignificance: A single word for what cannot be searched out carries no system of its own; its wonder is Paul's, that God's judgments have a depth no mind can sound.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
